title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-12-04
lineage: shn > wav > iZotope RX 6 Advanced > iZotope Ozone 5 Advanced > CD Wave > flac 16; edited and remastered SIRMick
source: Source: possibly SBD > cassette > ? > DAT > CD; CD > EAC > WAV > mkwACT > SHN - SHN conversion by Julian Fowler, May 2002;

ai_review.summary: A mixed‑quality soundboard of the Dec 1969 show that’s historically notable – first live Black Peter and Uncle John’s Band with vocals, plus a spooky Dark Star > High Time sequence.
ai_review.review: The performance captures a pivotal moment in late‑1969 Dead history, featuring the debut live renditions of Black Peter and Uncle John's Band (with full vocals) and a mammoth Dark Star that many reviewers call “spooky” and “primal.” The tape suffers from hiss, occasional drop‑outs and other defects, though recent restoration work by SIR Mick & Julian Fowler has markedly improved clarity; the early part of the show is ragged but the latter 80 minutes are strong.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality ranges from historically significant and musically exciting (Dark Star, first Black Peter/Uncle John’s Band) to a few reviewers calling it dismal; recording quality is mixed with noted tape defects but also praised restoration. Weighted average yields ~3.4 stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers note tape hiss, drop‑outs and other sound‑quality defects, but recent SIR Mick/Julian Fowler recovery greatly reduces the degradation; overall clarity is acceptable but not pristine.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The concert starts a bit ragged and disjointed, but from Dark Star onward the band settles into a primal Dead groove that showcases their transition from late‑60s psychedelia to the emerging Workingman's Dead era.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Now playing a Fender Stratocaster; his tone on Dark Star is highlighted as spooky and excellent.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass described as slugging, Jack Casady‑like, providing strong low‑end drive.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s “rosy fills” and tape‑hiss ambience are noted, underscoring the 60s psychedelic vibe.
band_member_comments.Drums: Seesaw‑style drumming is mentioned as part of the show’s characteristic feel.
